cards: Louis the Pious was the son and successor of Charlemagne, ruling the Carolingian Empire from 814 to 840.
Lothair I was the eldest son of Louis the Pious and Carolingian emperor from 840 to 855.
Charles the Bald was the youngest son of Louis the Pious.
Rurik was a Varangian chieftain who, according to the Primary Chronicle, was invited in 862 by Slavic and Finnic tribes of the north to rule them, settling at Ladoga and then Novgorod.
Ansgar was a Frankish monk and missionary, known as the Apostle of the North.
Louis the German was a son of Louis the Pious and king of East Francia.
Árpád was the leader of the Hungarian tribal federation who, after his father Álmos, led the Hungarians across the Carpathians into the Carpathian Basin around 895.
Kenneth MacAlpin was a king of Gaelic origin who became ruler of the Picts around 843.
Charles the Fat was a Carolingian ruler who briefly reunited the realms of the Carolingian Empire between 881 and 888 CE.
Egbert was king of Wessex from 802 to 839.
Einhard was a Frankish scholar and courtier at the court of Charlemagne.
Al-Khwarizmi was a Persian mathematician, astronomer and geographer who worked in Baghdad during the Abbasid Caliphate in the ninth century.
Rhodri the Great, Rhodri Mawr, was king of Gwynedd from 844 who also gained Powys and Seisyllwg, ruling most of Wales.
Zhu Wen was a Chinese military leader who first fought as a rebel under Huang Chao and then served the Tang Dynasty before turning against it.
Boso was a Frankish noble who in 879 became the first king outside the Carolingian family since 751.
Askold and Dir were rulers of Kiev in the 9th century, described in the Primary Chronicle as Varangians who took the city from the Khazars' tributaries and led a raid on Constantinople in 860.
Gudfred was a king of the Danes in the early 9th century and an opponent of Charlemagne.
Krum was khan of the First Bulgarian Empire from about 803 to 814.
Mihira Bhoja (Bhoja I) was the most powerful king of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, ruling from Kannauj from about 836 to 885.
Musa ibn Musa was the most powerful member of the Banu Qasi, a family of Muwallad lords in the upper Ebro valley.
Nikephoros I was a Byzantine emperor of the early ninth century.
r. 802–811 CE · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Nominoe was the first ruler of a united Brittany, a Breton noble and count of Vannes whom Louis the Pious appointed as his representative there in 831.
Wilfred the Hairy was Count of Urgell and Cerdanya from 870 and of Barcelona and Girona from 878, ruling most of the Catalan counties of the Spanish March.
Alfonso III, called the Great, was King of Asturias from 866 to 910.
Erispoe was ruler of Brittany from 851 to 857, son of Nominoe.
Halfdan the Black was a king of Vestfold in south-eastern Norway, known only from later sagas, above all Snorri Sturluson's Heimskringla.
Huang Chao was a failed examination candidate and salt smuggler who led the largest rebellion of the late Tang dynasty.
Íñigo Arista was the first king of Pamplona, the kingdom later known as Navarre.
Louis II of Italy was the eldest son of Lothair I, king of Italy from 844 and Carolingian emperor from 855.
Baldwin I of Flanders, called Iron Arm, was the first count of Flanders.
Bořivoj I is the first historically attested Duke of Bohemia of the Přemyslid dynasty.
Hermenegildo Gutiérrez was a Galician noble in the service of Alfonso III of Asturias.
Lothair II was the second son of Emperor Lothair I and received the northern part of Middle Francia at the Treaty of Prüm in 855, a kingdom later named Lotharingia after him.
Louis the Younger was king of East Francia from 876 to 882, a son of Louis the German.
Nicholas I Mystikos was Patriarch of Constantinople from 901 to 907 and again from 912 until his death.
Omurtag was khan of the First Bulgarian Empire from 814 to 831.
Vímara Peres was a vassal of King Alfonso III of Asturias who took the town of Portucale, modern Porto, from the Moors in 868.
Zhang Yichao was a local leader of Dunhuang who in 848 drove out the Tibetan garrison as the Tibetan Empire disintegrated, and went on to free other towns of the Hexi Corridor.
Ziryab, born Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Nafi, was a musician and singer from Baghdad who settled at the court of Abd al-Rahman II in Córdoba in 822.
Abbas ibn Firnas was an Andalusi polymath of Berber descent at the court of the Umayyad emirs of Córdoba in the ninth century.
